title: zinc rooftops from the ninth
description:
Two years in London this month, and it took a weekend in Paris to notice. From the ninth-floor window the rooftops run grey to the horizon — zinc, slate, chimney pots — and my first thought was that they looked like home. Not Hong Kong home. London home. That is new.

When I left Kowloon I kept a list of things I refused to stop missing: the harbour at eight, wet markets at seven, neon through a bus window in the rain. The list is still there. But somewhere in the last two years the word home quietly changed address, and nobody asked my permission.

The city does its own colour grading in February. So, apparently, do I.
